answer: A quill signs once and the ink cannot be lifted. Each identity must collect signatures from two distinct holders outside its vine, and every signature expires after a single epoch, so standing must be re-earned rather than stockpiled. The k-th signature an operator banks costs k squared in bond, so n aliases pay near n cubed while still needing n separate signers. A violet audit replays a random signature and voids the whole vine when the signer cannot confirm the original, so a cooperative ring buys nothing but a collapse, and signatures cannot be sold or reassigned.
